questions.question_text: Convert $5$ hours $15$ minutes to hours in decimal form.

options.why: Wrote the minutes straight after the decimal point instead of dividing $15$ by $60$.
Recognised $15$ min as a quarter but then wrote a half hour instead of $0.25$.
Divided $60$ by $15$ and read the $4$ as tenths of an hour.

questions.question_text: Convert $2$ hours $50$ minutes to hours in decimal form.

options.why: Copied the minutes after the decimal point instead of dividing $50$ by $60$.
Converted the $50$ minutes correctly but dropped the $2$ whole hours.
Divided $60$ by $50$ instead of $50$ by $60$, giving $1.2$ extra hours.

questions.question_text: Convert $3.4$ hours to hours and minutes.

options.why: Read the digit after the point as $40$ minutes instead of multiplying $0.4$ by $60$.
Read the digit after the point as $4$ minutes, leaving out the $\times60$ altogether.
Multiplied $0.4$ by $60$ but then subtracted $10$ instead of leaving the product alone.
Read $0.45$ h as $45$ minutes instead of multiplying $0.45$ by $60$.
Multiplied by $10$ rather than by $60$ when changing hours to minutes.
Added a whole hour that is not in the given time before converting.

questions.question_text: Convert $200$ minutes to hours in decimal form.

options.why: Took the $3$ whole hours and wrote the leftover $20$ minutes after the decimal point.
Divided $200$ by $100$ instead of by $60$, treating time as a decimal system.
Divided by $3600$, the number of seconds in an hour, instead of by $60$.

questions.question_text: Convert $2$ hours $6$ minutes $36$ seconds to hours in decimal form.

options.why: Converted the $6$ minutes but ignored the $36$ seconds altogether.
Divided the seconds by $60$ rather than $3600$, adding $0.6$ instead of $0.01$.
Wrote the minutes and seconds digits after the point without dividing at all.

questions.question_text: Convert $3.605$ hours to hours, minutes and seconds.

options.why: Rounded the leftover $0.3$ of a minute to half a minute instead of $0.3\times60$.
Read the digits $60$ and $5$ straight off as minutes and seconds.
Read each digit after the point as its own unit without multiplying by $60$.

questions.solution_text:
$3.605\text{ h}$
$=3\text{ h}+0.605\times60\text{ min}$
$=3\text{ h}+36.3\text{ min}$
$=3\text{ h }36\text{ min}+0.3\times60\text{ s}$
$=3\text{ h }36\text{ min }18\text{ s}$
